text: Henry Nolan’s motive to evoke nostalgia and a sense of belonging is directly linked to the thematic structure of his work through the use of the old mill as a central metaphor. By positioning the mill as a symbol of stability and resistance against modernity, Nolan structurally reinforces the importance of tradition and community. This thematic framework serves his intent by contrasting the enduring nature of the past with the disruptive forces of change, thereby encouraging readers to reflect on the value of their own heritage and communal ties in a rapidly evolving world.
